finding.claim: Broken authorization on the ban endpoint. The require_admin() call is wrapped in try/except Exception. abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException, which is an Exception subclass. The handler catches it, logs a warning, and carries on to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin user can therefore ban arbitrary users. The sibling handler unban() calls require_admin without the try/except, so it is enforced there.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban is the entry; uid comes from the URL
require_admin(g.user) is called; for a non-admin it runs abort(403) at line 11
except Exception catches the HTTPException raised by abort
The handler only logs a warning and does not return or re-raise

finding.guards_checked: require_admin checks is_admin and aborts with 403, but the exception is swallowed so the guard has no effect on ban(). unban() at admin.py:26 calls require_admin outside any try/except, so it is SAFE. There is no other middleware or before_request hook in the file. The only file in the repo is admin.py.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at admin.py:9-11 (aborts with 403 for non-admins), but its call at admin.py:17 is wrapped in try/except Exception at 16-19. No before_request hook, middleware, or decorator exists in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:16-20, the HTTPException from abort(403) (line 11) is caught by `except Exception` at line 18 and only logged, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for any non-admin user, unlike unban() at line 26, which calls require_admin outside a try/except.
